title: Buying Your First Soccer Ball
description: A shop assistant helps a customer choose a soccer ball and a pair of shoes for playing on the weekend.
transcript: Hi, welcome to the sports shop! Are you looking for something today? Great. You want a soccer ball, right? First, let's look at these balls on the shelf. This one is small. This one is a bit bigger. For playing on the weekend, I think this medium size is good. It is light and easy to kick. Now, let's find shoes for you. What size do you wear? Okay, size eight. Here are some shoes with small bumps on the bottom. These are called cleats. They help you stand still on the grass. Try them on. How do they feel? Good. They are comfortable, and they are not too expensive. So, one ball and one pair of shoes. That is a great start for your first game. Have fun playing this weekend!

questions.Question: What kind of shoes does the shop recommend, and what are the bumps on the bottom called?
questions.Answer: Shoes with small bumps on the bottom, called cleats
Options: Shoes with small bumps on the bottom, called cleats

Slippers with padding, called treads

It is for playing on the weekend and is light and easy to kick.
It is the largest ball, so it is easier to see on the grass.
It is the smallest ball, which is best for practicing indoors.

title: Match Day at the Park
description: Two friends meet at the park before their local soccer game and talk about the weather and who will be the goalkeeper.
transcript: Hi, it is a nice day at the park today. The sun is out and the sky is blue. I like this kind of weather. Today we have a soccer game with our local team. I am very happy about it. I think it will be a good game. Who will be our goalkeeper? I hope it is Tom. He is very good at stopping the ball. Let's go to the field now. We will have a lot of fun.

To express a personal hope and justify it, signalling a preference for Tom as goalkeeper

title: The Offside Rule
description: A coach explains to a new player, in simple words, when a player is offside and why the referee blows the whistle.
transcript: Hi, welcome! Today we talk about the offside rule. It can seem hard, but it is simple. Listen carefully. A player is offside when they are closer to the other team's goal line than the ball and the second last defender. So, look at the field. Is the attacker ahead of the defenders? If yes, they may be offside. But wait! A player is not offside in their own half. Also, they are not offside if they get the ball directly from a throw-in, a goal kick, or a corner. Now, why does the referee blow the whistle? Because the offside rule stops players from waiting near the goal for an easy pass. When the referee sees an offside player who is active in the play, the referee stops the game and gives a free kick to the other team. Good job! Remember, be onside, stay with the defenders, and you will be fine.

questions.Question: According to the transcript, when is a player NOT offside?
questions.Answer: When they are in their own half
Options: When they are in their own half
When they are closer to the goal line than the ball
When they are ahead of the second last defender
When they are waiting near the goal for a pass

questions.Question: According to the transcript, which two situations mean a player cannot be offside even when they are ahead of the defenders?
questions.Answer: When the player is in their own half, or when they receive the ball directly from a throw-in, a goal kick, or a corner
Options: When the player is in their own half, or when they receive the ball directly from a throw-in, a goal kick, or a corner
When the player is closer to the goal line than the ball, or when the referee blows the whistle
When the player waits near the goal for an easy pass, or when the referee gives a free kick
When the player stays with the defenders, or when the ball is passed from a teammate in the attacking half

questions.Question: Why does the speaker explain why the referee blows the whistle?
questions.Answer: To show that the rule has a clear purpose
Options: To show that the rule has a clear purpose
To complain about how referees work
To change the offside definition
To explain how teams score goals

title: My Favourite Player
description: A young fan describes her favourite soccer player, where he plays, and why she likes watching his goals.
transcript: Hi, my name is Mia, and I am ten years old. My favourite player is Leo. He plays soccer for a big team in the city. He is very fast. He has a red shirt with the number ten. When he runs with the ball, I watch him closely. Sometimes he kicks the ball into the net. That is a goal! I jump up and clap my hands. My dad says that Leo is the best. I think so too. I like his goals because they are fun to watch. Now I want to play soccer like him.

She admires him and sees him as a role model she wants to imitate.

description: A teenager practises free throws alone in the driveway and counts how many baskets she makes out of ten.
transcript: Hi, my name is Mia. Today I practise free throws. I go to the driveway. I have a ball and a hoop. I take ten shots. I throw the ball. Some balls go in. Some balls do not. I count the baskets. I make six baskets. That is good. I am happy.

title: Team Tryouts
description: Two students talk after school about trying out for the basketball team and what the coach asked them to do.
transcript: Hi, I'm Sam. Today was a big day for me. After school, I went to the gym for basketball tryouts. There were many students there. I was a little nervous. The coach blew his whistle and said, "Okay, everyone, listen." First, we ran around the court. Then we did some passing drills. Next, the coach asked us to shoot free throws. I made four out of ten. After that, we played a short game. At the end, the coach said he would post the team list on Friday. I hope I made it. Wish me luck!

title: Going to a Basketball Game
description: A father and son buy tickets, walk to the arena, and talk about which team they want to win tonight.
transcript: Hi, I am Tom, and today is a big day. My son Ben and I are going to a basketball game tonight. First, we stop at the box office. We buy two tickets. Then we walk to the arena. It is not far. Ben is very excited. He talks about the game. He says, "Dad, I want the Eagles to win." I smile. I say, "Well, I want the Tigers to win." Ben laughs. We walk and talk. It is a cold night, but we are happy. Soon we see the big arena lights. We are almost there. Let's go!
